## Description

A large disc-shaped desmid (200–400 × 190–270 µm) shaped like a flat star with deeply cut lobes, of
acid peat bogs and marshes; one of the most beautiful cells under the microscope. Two semicells of
five lobes each.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: `pond` (weight 0.15), `puddle` (weight 0.15); 1 individuals in a reference drop at weight 1.
<!-- /GENERATED -->

A [silhouette](../../mechanics/shape-changes.md) with the deep narrow sinus of the isthmus and, in each semicell,
wedge-shaped incisions between the polar lobe and the lateral ones (±35°) and those that split each
lateral lobe in two (±64°). Incisions are shallower and slightly wider than the real ones (walls
closer than ~3 membrane points crossed when dividing). After division the new semicell
[regrows from the isthmus](../../mechanics/shape-changes.md) over a few hours.

## Literature

- Kreutz M., realmicrolife.com (size, lobes).
- Meindl U. (1993) Microbiol. Rev. 57: 415–433 (semicell morphogenesis; time estimated).

## Not implemented yet

- Toothed lobe margins (finer than the membrane) are not drawn.
- Morphogenesis is a timed shape interpolation, not regulated growth of the primary wall.
- No measured µmax.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares semicell regrowth and notches with *Cosmarium*.
